observations: The page number «88» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01: «ἀναπλήρωσις» completes the sentence that ends p. 87 (JP2 0119, L29), «das wiederum dem ptolemäischen»; the Greek in italics, with the smooth breathing on the first α and the acute on the η; ἔμπτωσις, μονή and ἀναπλήρωσις are Ptolemy's words for the immersion, the totality and the emersion of a lunar eclipse.

Between L15 and L16 two figures side by side; they are not reproduced; L16 has their captions, «Fig. 3.» and «Fig. 4.», each centred under its figure. Fig. 3: a large semicircle, the earth's shadow, on a base line E S K, S its centre; a vertical line from S to the top of the semicircle, with N on it; the small circle of the moon about M at the upper right, outside the semicircle, which crosses the lower left part of the small circle; the horizontal line N M and the line S M. Fig. 4: the same semicircle with E, S and K, the vertical line from S with N on it; the small circle about M inside the semicircle, touching it at P at the upper right; the horizontal line N M and the line from S through M and P to T outside the semicircle. The letters are italic.

L03-L15 and N01-N02. Checked: with R the radius of the shadow, r that of the moon and SN the latitude of the moon, the moon's centre at the first contact lies at MS = R + r from S (Fig. 3, where the drawing shows the circles overlapping rather than touching), and MN = √((R + r)² − SN²) is the arc of the moon's path to the middle of the eclipse; at the beginning of totality (Fig. 4) SM = R − r = ST − MT, with ST = R + r and MT = 2r, or SP − MP (note 1), and MN = √((R − r)² − SN²) is the arc to the middle; divided by the moon's hourly motion relative to the shadow they give casus with half mora, and half mora; their difference is the casus.

L17-L30. Checked: 20′ 43″ = 20 43/60 : 60 = 0.3453; 58′ × 0.345 = 20.0′, «0 dig. 20′»; 5′ 6″ × 0.345 = 1′ 45.6″, «1′ 46″»; 6′ 6″ × 0.345 = 2′ 6.3″, «2′ 6″»; 19 dig. 16′ + 20′ = 19 dig. 36′; 29′ 39″ + 1′ 46″ = 31′ 25″; 21′ 2″ + 2′ 6″ = 23′ 8″. The proportion 0.345 at the corrected anomaly 285° 45′ (74° 15′ from the apogee) is the fraction of the way from the greatest to the least distance of the moon on an epicycle of radius 5p 10′ (p. 46, JP2 0078): the distance √(60² + 5;10² + 2 · 60 · 5;10 · cos 74° 15′) = 61p 36′ lies 0.3448 of the way from 65p 10′ to 54p 50′, 20′ 41″ in sixtieths, where (1 − cos 74° 15′) : 2 would give 21′ 51″. The values of Tables 73, 74 and 76 are to be compared with the tables. With the corrected argument of latitude 359° 11′ 53″ (p. 85) the latitude of the moon is about 3′ 47″ south, so that the eclipse is nearly central.

L24: «20 43/60 ∶ 60», the case fraction written {cf:43|60}, the colon of the division with a word space on either side (21 px), written ∶ (U+2236). L26 and L30: «0dig. 20′», «19dig. 36′», the abbreviation raised in the smaller type; the values set in three columns under the heads of L29 and of p. 87 (JP2 0119, L01); L29 in the smaller type, with a colon after «Mora», where p. 87 has a full stop. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|».
L05, L06, L12: «MS2», «SN2», «SM2», the 2 raised and upright. The dashes: L04 «5—14», the long dash set close; L09 «zusammen). — Zweitens», the long dash with a space on either side.

Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.»; italics: the Greek word, «emersio», «respiratio.», «Casus», «Mora», «halbe Mora», the letters of the figures, «Tabula proportionis.», «Anomalia aequata», «dakaicae superationum».
The other colons and the semicolon stand after the thin space of the edition (8-14 px measured).
